analysis:
The PR modifies only docs/architecture/inference.md. The changed range (base 2058-2069, head 2058-2077) sits in the Native Flint section. No code, config or wire-contract changes are present, so no runtime security control is altered by this diff.

The documented change says Flint now always uses native KV and native checkpoint precision, ignoring provider-wide defaults. It refuses explicit non-native selections. It forces paged attention: an automatic backend selection is treated as explicit paged, and an explicit contiguous selection, the paged kill switch or a model-capability veto refuses the load. All of this is claimed for EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.resolve and EngineV2Factory.prepareProductionBackend.

Threat-model relevance:
- T-041 (prefix-cache and SSD tier) and T-028/T-010 (availability) are only indirectly touched. Native checkpoint precision for Flint changes nothing about the encrypted SSD storage posture. The HMAC names, 30-minute TTL and KEK scoping described in T-041 are not mentioned or altered here.
- A load refusal when paged is unavailable is fail-closed. It is an availability tradeoff, not a confidentiality regression.

The patch excerpt is truncated and the rest of the new text is not visible. The corresponding Swift code changes (EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy, EngineV2Factory+BackendPreparation) are not in this batch. I cannot verify that the documentation matches the implementation. If the implementation changed how Flint interacts with SSD checkpoint storage or paged-prefix encrypted store paths, integration should check that T-041 posture (cacheSalt scoping, per-donation gating) is preserved. I identified no concrete regression or threat-model invalidation from the supplied documentation alone.
